title: The Usual seat by the window
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：usual　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 usual 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1952 the tailor wrote of ① a usual seat by the window in the order, and everybody in the shop said at once that it was ② so usual that nobody in the shop would go near it. Three weeks on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the tailor, who never explained anything, had done it before dawn and gone home; it was the usual ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the usual seat by the window that anybody there had ever seen, or so the order for November 1946 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too usual to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the customer who had come to help; the usual ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the needle at the far mirror, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a usual hour for the walk, and said that no customer in his right mind would call it ⑥ as usual as the hour for the walk they had once had in the old shop. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was usual or not, and he said so.

By 1959 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the order. What the line asked for was ⑦ something usual, and nothing besides. The customer from the next shop called the whole plan ⑧ quite usual; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the order kept the names of the usual ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1962, in public, she wrote of another usual seat by the window in the same order, and the work, which took two weeks, seemed ⑨ no less usual than anybody had expected. ⑩ The usual hour for the walk that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1964, was the one she could never quite name; the usual ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 通常（前置定语 a usual seat by the window：1952 年裁缝在订单簿里记下的那件通常的座位）
B. adj. 通常／惯常（两处加强说法：so usual that … 与 no less usual than …）
C. adj. 通常／惯常（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 通常（表语 too usual to do：母亲觉得它太通常，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 惯常（前置定语 a usual hour for the walk：叔叔把整件事称作一桩惯常的时辰）
F. adj. 惯常（同级比较 as usual as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩照例散步的时辰相比）
G. adj. 惯常（后置定语 something usual：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 惯常（受程度副词修饰 quite usual：那位顾客的评价）

items.q: a usual seat by the window
the usual seat by the window that
a usual hour for the walk
The usual hour for the walk that

answers.why: usual 意为“通常”，1952 年裁缝在订单簿里记下的是“一件通常的座位”，此处作前置定语 a usual seat by the window。
usual 意为“通常”，此处用 so usual that 结构，说它通常到裁缝铺里没人敢靠近。
usual 意为“通常”，订单簿上 十一月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的通常窗边惯常的座位，等于最高级的说法。
usual 意为“通常”，母亲认为这件东西“太通常了，谁也用不上”，too usual to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
usual 意为“惯常”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩惯常的时辰”，此处作前置定语 a usual hour for the walk。
usual 意为“惯常”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩照例散步的时辰一样惯常”，同级比较用 as usual as。
usual 意为“惯常”，订单簿上那半行字要的是“惯常的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something usual。
usual 意为“惯常”，邻裁缝铺来的那位顾客认为这套计划“相当惯常”，quite 修饰原级 usual。
usual 意为“惯常”，no less usual than 表示“其惯常不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之惯常不亚于任何人的预料。
usual 意为“惯常”，母亲 1964 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的惯常时辰”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1952 年，裁缝在订单簿里记下了一件通常的座位。（a usual seat by the window）
它通常到裁缝铺里没有一个人敢靠近。（so usual that …）
母亲觉得它太通常，谁也用不上。（too usual to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩惯常的时辰。（a usual hour for the walk）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩照例散步的时辰一样惯常。（as usual as …）
到了 1959 年，订单簿上只剩半行字：要的是一件惯常的东西。（something usual）
answers: In 1952 the tailor wrote of a usual seat by the window in the order.
It was so usual that nobody in the shop would go near it.
My mother thought it too usual to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a usual hour for the walk.
He said nobody would call it as usual as the hour for the walk they had once had.
By 1959 the order asked for nothing but something usual.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 usual 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1952 the tailor wrote of a usual seat by the window in the order, and nobody forgot it.
It was the usual seat by the window that anybody there had ever seen, or so the order says.
My mother thought it too usual to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a usual hour for the walk, and nobody argued with him.
The customer from the next shop called the plan quite usual, and everybody laughed.
The usual ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
